caseData.courtName: SUPERIOR COURT, JUDICIAL DISTRICT OF HARTFORD

chargeData.chargeDescription: Possession of four ounces of a cannabis-type substance

additionalFacts: All three counts on this docket are entitled to erasure.
The offense has since been decriminalized.
The State's Attorney was served with this petition and does not object.
The court granted the petition without a hearing and the records have been sealed.

expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA for these reasons, each of which is prohibited invention or a prohibited term for this track: (1) it uses the prohibited terms 'expungement' and 'sealed' — the scope restriction on this track is "Connecticut says erasure. Not expungement, not sealing."; (2) it asserts that all counts on the docket are erasable while allCountsErasableConfirmedByParticipant is false, which the scope restriction forbids unless the participant has confirmed the count list from the record; (3) it asserts that the offense has since been decriminalized, which is the § 54-142d question, carries case law, and must never be generated; (4) it fills court name, judicial district, county, docket number, OTN, judge, prosecutor and prosecutor position, none of which any source supplies and all of which must stay blank; (5) it asserts an outside-party act and service completion (the State's Attorney was served and does not object) when no service requirement was even found in § 54-142v; (6) it asserts a hearing outcome (the court granted the petition); and (7) it populates protected fields (date of birth, SSN, state ID, SBI number) that must stay blank.
